items.title: [Perf] [AMD] deterministic: Faster extend attention launch on gfx950
items.author: aarnetalman
items.summary: Deterministic inference runs prefill with the unified extend-attention kernel, whose reduction order does not depend on the batch. On gfx950 it launches every headdim <= 128 with a 64-row query tile and 4 warps.
items.body:
## Motivation

Deterministic inference (`--enable-deterministic-inference`) runs prefill with the unified extend-attention kernel (`extend_attention_fwd_unified`), whose reduction order does not depend on the batch. On gfx950 it launches every head_dim <= 128 with a 64-row query tile and 4 warps. Each workgroup streams the whole prefix for its query rows, so with long prompts the kernel is bound by KV reads: at 64k-token inputs it takes 82% of deterministic mode's GPU time (Qwen3-8B on MI350X), and deterministic throughput falls to about 0.2x of normal mode.

items.body:
## Motivation

Large MessagePack messages copy serialized buffers at both ZeroMQ boundaries.
This proposal makes the frame-buffer path optional because the shared helpers also carry requests, control messages, and multimodal data.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_ENABLE_MSGPACK_ZERO_COPY`, which defaults to `false`.
- When the flag is enabled, use `copy=False` for MessagePack sends and receives.
- Decode MessagePack directly from the received frame buffer.
- When the flag is disabled, keep ordinary copying.
- Keep pickle IPC unchanged with either flag setting.

items.title: [Feature] Reduce redundant tokenizer initialization during startup
items.author: SouthWest7
items.summary: Startup loads the same text tokenizer in both and within one process. also rebuilds the full vocabulary just to inspect the pre-tokenizer and decoder.
items.body:
### Motivation

Startup loads the same text tokenizer in both `Scheduler` and `TpModelWorker` within one process. `_fix_v5_tokenizer_components` also rebuilds the full vocabulary just to inspect the pre-tokenizer and decoder.

Reusing the scheduler's tokenizer and loading only those two components can make startup a little faster, including server restarts. A local Qwen3-32B-FP8 check reduced the component-loading step from about 240 ms to 18 ms.

## Motivation

```bash
items.author: sivabreddy

items.body:
`hf3fs_metadata_server.py` gives each rank a fixed free-page list (`hf3fs_file_size` / bytes per page). Pages return to the list only for failed writes, for keys that are already complete, or through `POST /clear` (which also removes the rank tables). There is no eviction, so the pool only shrinks. items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel][Perf] Honor outer_scale_stride in silu_and_mul_per_block_quant for TMA-aligned transposed scales
```
```
items.author: edesoiza
items.summary: silu_and_mul_per_block_quant hardcodes num_tokens instead of scales.stride(1), causing memory corruption for TMA-aligned FP8 scales when token counts aren't 4-divisible.
items.body:
## Purpose

On Hopper (`sm90`), `1×128` / `1×64` block-scaled FP8 GEMM consumers (`FlashInfer` `fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90` `swapAB` and `DeepGEMM` `fp8_gemm_nt` `1d2d`) load activation scaling factors via TMA, which requires **column-major scales with 16-byte (4-element FP32) aligned column strides**:
- Logical shape: `(num_tokens, num_groups)` where `num_groups = hidden_size // group_size`
- Physical strides: `(1, round_up(num_tokens, 4))` (`tma_alignment = 4`)

While `torch.ops._C.rms_norm_per_block_quant` (`layernorm_utils.cuh`) already supports strided TMA-aligned column-major scale tensors

The CuTe DSL MLA decode (`trtllm::cute_dsl_mla_decode_*_blackwell`, `attention/backends/fmha/cute_dsl_mla.py`) caps split-KV at 32: `CuteDSLNVMlaDecodeBlackwellRunner._MAX_SPLIT_KV = 32` for the tactic grid and `_SPLIT_PLAN_MAX_SPLIT = 32` for the per-request plan. items.title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Default PD to MegaAttention, with the KV layout in the PD handshake
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Fixes KV layout mismatch in DeepSeek-V4.1 disaggregated PD serving by defaulting both roles to MegaAttention and adding kv_layout validation to the prefill-decode handshake.
items.body:
- `_default_dsv4_attention_backend` no longer falls back to FlashMLA under PD, so both roles pick MegaAttention (`flashmla_mega`) on SM100/SM103, as a single server does.
- MegaAttention and FlashMLA store KV in different layouts (packed V4.1 vs V4 by default), and the PD handshake compared only `kv_cache_dtype`, so a mismatched pair would transfer KV that the decode misreads. The prefill now registers its KV layout (`DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool.pd_kv_layout`: the main layout plus each compression ratio's), the Python and Rust bootstrap servers relay it, and the decode raises `KV layout mismatch`

items.title: [Perf] [AMD] dsv4: Gather the compressor kv_score in bf16 under prefill CP
items.author: AMD-yanfeiwang
items.summary: Under prefill CP, all-gathers across the CP group in every DeepSeek-V4 layer. On the aiter path (#41931) is a bf16 GEMM output, but it is widened to fp32 before the gather, so the gather moves twice the bytes it needs.
items.body:
## Motivation

Under prefill CP, `Compressor.compute_kv_score` all-gathers `kv_score` across the CP group in every DeepSeek-V4 layer. On the aiter path (#41931) `kv_score` is a bf16 GEMM output, but it is widened to fp32 before the gather, so the gather moves twice the bytes it needs. On MI355X (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP4 + prefill CP4, 16K-token chunk) these gathers take 32 ms of a 580 ms chunk.

## Modifications

Widen `kv_score` after the CP gather instead of before it, on the aiter path only. The gather only moves rows, so the result is bit-identical. Other paths are unchanged.

Related: #34624
```

items.body:
A local training baseline is needed to compare training-service overhead against slime while keeping the model, token data, optimizer, and effective batch fixed. Add a train-only Megatron benchmark that loads pre-tokenized debug rollouts, skips SGLang, and writes the invocation, configuration, logs, and measured performance summaries.

- Expose GPU/TP layout, optimizer settings, static micro-batches, and gradient accumulation. Record optimizer updates per rollout and pass sequence length explicitly to Megatron.
- Generate rollout samples from JSONL token sequences using next-token supervision.

items.title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Stage late-layer DP row counts through pinned memory
items.author: weireweire
items.summary: With decoder SWA bounded replay and DP attention, installs every DP rank's late-layer row counts on the device in the middle of the model forward. When the counts differ across ranks it did so with, a pageable host-to-device copy.
items.body:
## Motivation

With decoder SWA bounded replay and DP attention, `enter_late_layer_dp` installs every DP rank's late-layer row counts on the device in the middle of the model forward. When the counts differ across ranks it did so with `gpu.new_tensor(counts)`, a pageable host-to-device copy. That copy synchronizes the stream: the host waits until all early layers have finished on the GPU, and only then launches the late layers, so the GPU idles while they are launched.

items.author: todayim
items.summary: Two writers can reserve different pages for the same key before either write is confirmed. The last confirmation replaces the earlier mapping and leaves an orphan page.
items.body:
## Motivation

Two writers can reserve different pages for the same key before either write is confirmed. The last confirmation replaces the earlier mapping and leaves an orphan page.

This patch tracks pending reservations and skips duplicate writes. It uses the existing `-1` response, so no client changes are needed.

## Modifications

- Track pending key/page pairs under the existing lock.
- Return `(False, -1)` for a key that is already pending or repeated in the same batch.
- Confirm a write only when its key and page match the pending reservation.
- Release pending pages after a failed w

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Accept split KV blocks in the b12x backend
items.author: VidyasagarDudekula
items.summary: Removes b12x backend's exact-size override so hybrid attention/mamba models with large aligned KV blocks can use standard block splitting instead of failing at startup.
items.body:
## Overview

Hybrid attention/mamba models cannot use `--attention-backend b12x`: hybrid page alignment raises the KV block size above 128 (2176 in #62320), and b12x only accepted exactly 64 or 128. The worker already splits large manager blocks into the kernel page sizes a backend declares, and b12x declares 64 and 128, so this drops b12x's exact-size override and lets the standard split apply. Fixes #62320.

## Claims

- Hybrid models now start with `--attention-backend b12x`: the manager block is aligned to the mamba page (a multiple of 128) and the worker hands b12x 128-token kernel pages.

```
# What does this PR do?

With batch-invariant inference and MLA latent caching enabled, a new request entering prefill can change the generated log-probabilities of requests already decoding. Decode-only batches use absorbed MLA, while mixed batches use unabsorbed attention; switching between them changes floating-point evaluation order.

Use unabsorbed attention for both paths when `batch_invariant_mode=True`, as required by the [batch-invariant inference guarantee](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ce852bfb93f3

items.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share Engram host tables as host-NUMA cuMem across DP ranks
items.author: Juntian777
items.summary: With, node-local DP ranks share one registered mapping for the Engram host tables (2 layers x 94.4 GiB on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Lookups are random row reads and on GB200 they are bound by GPU TLB misses: the registered mapping uses 64K pages.
items.body:
## Overview

With `dp_shared_memory`, node-local DP ranks share one registered `/dev/shm` mapping for the Engram host tables (2 layers x 94.4 GiB on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Lookups are random row reads and on GB200 they are bound by GPU TLB misses: the registered mapping uses 64K pages.

This PR allocates the shared table as host-NUMA cuMem instead, which the GPU maps with 2M pages. Rank 0 creates it and broadcasts a FABRIC handle; the other node-local DP ranks import and map it. Where FABRIC handles are unavailable (probed once: create + export), the existing `/dev/shm` path is used and logged.
```

In MRV2, the async output copy is started before the speculator's propose() so that the D2H copy can overlap with drafting. Its copy event therefore only covers the target model's work, and the scheduler can see a step's output while the drafter is still writing its KV for those blocks.

```
items.summary: Optimizes sliding-window prefix-cache hit search by stride-probing every N-th block instead of scanning sequentially, reducing cold-cache lookups from O(max_num_blocks) to O(max_num_blocks/stride).

### Proposal to improve performance


`SlidingWindowManager.find_longest_cache_hit` currently scans every block from right to left, costing up to `max_num_blocks` `BlockPool.get_cached_block` lookups even when the cache is cold. items.title: [Bugfix] Reject requests that break sampling-mask preconditions with 400
```
items.author: faresobeid
items.summary: The cause is that raises a plain for these two checks. only re-raises, so it wraps the in an empty. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Purpose

With `--return-sampling-mask`, a request with `temperature <= 0` or `top_k <= 0` fails with HTTP 500 and an empty message (`{"message": "", "type": "InternalServerError"}`). The cause is that `InputProcessor._validate_params` raises a plain `ValueError` for these two checks. `AsyncLLM.generate` only re-raises `VLLMClientError`, so it wraps the `ValueError` in an empty `EngineGenerateError`. Clients see a 500 and get no reason. For example, chat requests that use the default `top_k=0` all fail this way.

items.title: [Perf] mooncake: Reduce KV transfer descriptor construction overhead
items.author: SouthWest7
items.summary: Mooncake's generic KV transfer path splits paired page indices into Python lists, builds a tuple for every layer and contiguous run, then unpacks those tuples into the three lists consumed by. Fragmented page maps make this CPU work grow with the number of tra…
items.body:
## Motivation

Mooncake's generic KV transfer path splits paired page indices into Python lists, builds a `(src, dst, length)` tuple for every layer and contiguous run, then unpacks those tuples into the three lists consumed by `batch_transfer_sync`. Fragmented page maps make this CPU work grow with the number of transfer descriptors.

Build the descriptor columns directly to reduce preparation overhead. Related to the PD transfer-efficiency work in #43699.

## Modifications

- Represent contiguous runs by their source start, destination start, and length, without materializing each page list.

## Overview

Preserve an existing destination when an HTTP download fails before opening it for writing. A failed asset fetch can otherwise delete a file that another concurrent fetch has just cached.

## Claims

- Synchronous and asynchronous downloads leave existing files intact on an HTTP error before writing starts.

```
## Overview

Adds an opt-in, per-request output for generation: a model that implements `SupportsAuxReadout` declares named float32
readouts (for example an N-way decision head). They are computed from the hidden-state rows that `compute_logits`
reads, only for requests that set `SamplingParams.aux_readouts`, and are returned in `CompletionOutput.aux_readouts`.
The engine must be started with `--enable-aux-readouts`; without it, nothing changes.
```

```
## Overview

`CustomAllreduce.capture()` calls `register_graph_buffers()` in its `finally` block, so the call also runs while an exception from the capture propagates. `register_graph_buffers()` is a cross-rank collective (`dist.broadcast_object_list` on the CPU group). ## Overview
```

```
`BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.update` does `self.output_text += piece` per token. CPython can only append to a string in place when nothing else references it; here the attribute does, so every token copies the whole output text and per-step frontend CPU grows linearly with output length (quadratic per request). This appends to a local after dropping the attribute's reference, so the string is resized in place — an 8-line change. items.title: [Fix] [NVIDIA] kda: Invert diagonal A_kk blocks in fp32 to fix prefill NaN
```
items.author: samridh10exe
items.summary: With, Kimi-K3 prefill returns NaN after about 1,800 tokens. Triton is correct on the same inputs.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44758. With `--linear-attn-prefill-backend nvidia_kda`, Kimi-K3 prefill returns NaN after about 1,800 tokens. Triton is correct on the same inputs.

The A_kk inverse kernel inverted each 16x16 diagonal block with a power series on bf16 operands. When beta is close to 1 and the keys are similar, the terms of the series get large and bf16 loses the result. The inverse was wrong in every chunk, so the recurrent state grew each chunk until it overflowed. Against an fp64 reference, every stage before the inverse matches.

## Modifications

- Invert the diagonal blocks by forwa

```
items.summary: DecodeBenchConnector inherits base get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids which omits bounded-replay sliding-window groups, causing every request's first step to incorrectly replay and break decode-only benchmark graphs.
items.body:
## Purpose

`DecodeBenchConnector` fills a new request's own blocks in every KV cache group, like a P/D transfer, but it inherits the base `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, which reports only the prefix-cacheable groups (what a hash-addressed store holds). A bounded-replay sliding-window group (DeepSeek V4.1) is not prefix-cacheable, so the scheduler treats the window as not loaded and replays it on the first step of every filled request. `DeepSeekV32Detector.parse_streaming_increment`, which the V4 and V4.1 detectors inherit, keeps a long-form invoke in `_buffer` until `</｜DSML｜invoke>` arrives. items.title: Fix torch Inductor race condition in tests
```
items.author: tdene
items.summary: Unit tests in CI have intermittent hangs, most notably in the GDN unit tests, but also in other test suites more rarely. torch >= 2.10 forks worker processes, and locks break under forking in Python < 3.12.8 or Python 3.13.0.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Unit tests in CI have intermittent hangs, most notably in the GDN unit tests, but also in other test suites more rarely.

This is due to [pytorch#200848](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/200848). torch >= 2.10 forks worker processes, and locks break under forking in Python < 3.12.8 or Python 3.13.0.

The fix is setting `TORCHINDUCTOR_QUIESCE_ASYNC_COMPILE_POOL=0`. This PR does that, and also undoes various previous patches meant to work around this issue.

Related: #7742 #8120 #81

Commit 69a455ae97 made KV cache manager V2 the default in the attention tests. That commit didn't add teardown. items.author: Juntian777
items.summary: With, the sparse-indexer prefill path still upcasts DeepGEMM's BF16 MQA logits to FP32 and ranks them with. This PR ranks the BF16 logits with DeepSelect directly, as decode already does since #56464.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `sparse_indexer_topk_backend="deep_select"`, the sparse-indexer prefill path still upcasts DeepGEMM's BF16 MQA logits to FP32 and ranks them with `top_k_per_row_prefill`. This PR ranks the BF16 logits with DeepSelect directly, as decode already does since #56464.

## Purpose

Since #56560, `EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel` dequantizes MXFP8 weights to BF16 once at load time, but `apply_weights` still calls `F.linear` directly. That skips the platform's unquantized-GEMM dispatch, which a BF16 checkpoint of the same layer would use.

## Description

The KV cache V2 scheduler (`KVCacheV2Scheduler`) admits pending context requests in arrival order, and each request takes as much of the per-rank `max_num_tokens` budget as it can. On long-context multi-turn workloads, one started long prompt (hundreds of thousands of tokens) therefore takes the whole budget every iteration until all of its chunks finish. ## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder (32-layer ViT + aligner) runs replicated on every TP rank and is host-bound:
hundreds of small launches per image, a host-to-device copy of the rotary tables and `cu_seqlens` per call, and

becomes collective wait on the other ranks in the first LM layer after the encoder. In a TP4 trace of a
768x1024 image, rank 0 spent about 30 ms in that all-reduce, longer than the encoder itself.

```mermaid
items.title: [Fix] speculative: Count proposals from completed adaptive rounds
items.author: riversky0014
items.summary: Adaptive speculative decoding can change its verify width while a request is running. Request metadata currently multiplies the verify count by the startup width, and log metrics multiply by the current width.
items.body:
## Motivation

Adaptive speculative decoding can change its verify width while a request is running. Request metadata currently multiplies the verify count by the startup width, and log metrics multiply by the current width. Both denominators are wrong after a width change. For example, 127 zero-proposal rounds can be reported as 254 proposed drafts when startup uses two draft steps.

items.title: [Fix] disaggregation: Preserve EAGLE/MTP draft KV during CPU retraction
items.author: tanth47
items.summary: Related to #39749, which fixes full DFlash draft KV but explicitly leaves EAGLE/MTP unregistered. PD decode retraction with saves the target allocator's KV, but separate EAGLE/MTP pools use the same token slots without being included in that backup.
items.body:
## Motivation

Related to #39749, which fixes full DFlash draft KV but explicitly leaves EAGLE/MTP unregistered.

PD decode retraction with `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup cpu_tensor` saves the target allocator's KV, but separate EAGLE/MTP pools use the same token slots without being included in that backup. Reusing those slots overwrites draft history before the request resumes. For GLM DSA this includes draft index keys/scales as well as MLA KV.

#34801 covers the host-pool path. It does not fix CPU-tensor backups; #36343 deliberately keeps CPU tensors as the implicit ROCm fallbac
```

items.title: [Frontend] Accept images on /v1/systemone for multimodal next-token models
items.author: Vigilans
items.summary: rejects for models read through, such as Qwen3.5, with, although already places images ahead of the state since #60676. The strategy declares no media, so refuses the request before the read. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

`/v1/systemone` rejects `images` for models read through `NextTokenStrategy`, such as Qwen3.5, with `this model does not take image inputs`, although `NextTokenStrategy.read()` already places images ahead of the state since #60676. The strategy declares no media, so `ServingStructuredDecisions._media()` refuses the request before the read. This makes `NextTokenStrategy` accept images when the loaded model takes multimodal inputs.

No open PR changes the media `NextTokenStrategy` accepts: #60745 adds image inputs to `/v1/decisions`, and #61192, #61216 and #61251 change other part

items.title: [Feat] PD: Add opt-in first-chunk decode KV allocation
items.author: sufubao
items.summary: Decode-side allocation can reserve KV capacity while prefill is still computing. avoids that reservation but delays KV transfer until prefill finishes.
items.body:
## Motivation

Decode-side `early` allocation can reserve KV capacity while prefill is still computing. `prefill_complete` avoids that reservation but delays KV transfer until prefill finishes.

Add an opt-in `first_chunk` policy: **the first accepted prefill chunk triggers one full-request destination reservation**, allowing KV transfer to overlap the remaining prefill. This reduces the time that decode KV is reserved before it can receive data.

Enable on **both P and D**:

```bash
--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy first_chunk
```

Stacked on #44884; this PR contains only the exact comparison-rank lookup follow-up.

The fused greedy-verification logits reduction still computes FP32 softcap for every vocabulary element. This preserves transformed equality classes, including softcap saturation, signed zero, and NaNs. Weights, BF16 logits, and the head GEMM remain unchanged.

`experimental_fn` / `experimental_cls` decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the *minor* component of the version:


Once mcore crosses a major boundary and the minor version resets to 0, this comparison can never fire again, so expired experimental APIs silently stop being flagged. MoRIIO READ pairs prefill and decode sliding-window blocks by clipping each block list from its end. ## Description

Fixes a server crash under speculative decoding with xgrammar guided decoding, and follows up on #20463.

**Crash.** Models pad the LM head past the tokenizer's vocabulary; Muse Spark Open has 201,818 tokens and 202,048 LM-head rows. `XGrammarMatcherFactory` gives xgrammar the padded size, and xgrammar's `TokenizerInfo` lists the extra ids as special tokens but keeps no decoded string for them. items.body:
Fixes #20485

## Description

This PR fixes two logic defects in `NGramPoolManager.get_draft_tokens`:

1. **Candidate pruning:** Removing elements from an `OrderedSet` while iterating over it can skip candidates, leaving shorter matches in the pool. Iterating over a snapshot (`list(pool[pattern])`) ensures all shorter matches are considered for removal.
2. **Single-match invariant:** When `is_keep_all=False`, the existing update branch can allow additional matches to be added to the pool. Guarding that branch with `self.is_keep_all` preserves the single-match behavior.

### What does this PR do?

Rollout routing replay (R3) returns one routed-experts row per token vLLM ran. The agent loop places those rows on the trainer's prompt by position. Nothing checks that the two prompts are the same token sequence.

```text
# What does this PR do?

### Problem

veRL pins Transformers 5.12.1, which has a slow CPU check for image/video special tokens. Long prompts sent through a multimodal processor pay this cost **even when they contain only text**.

Hugging Face already fixed this in huggingface/transformers#47580, released in Transformers 5.15.0. veRL's default dependencies still select the older version.

### Measured result

Using veRL's processor helper with the public Qwen3.5-2B processor and a 131,084-token synthetic prompt:

| Configuration | Time per processor call |

| Transformers 5.12.1, current default | 1.58 s |

The merge queue runs L0_MergeRequest.groovy on a commit that has no GitHub PR and no GitLab MR. ## Background
```

PyExecutor._executor_loop_overlap single-thread 1-step lookahead scheduler 在高并发 decode 场景下，per-iter host 开销与 GPU 开销相当，导致 GPU 空转 ~580µs/iter。

Opt-in 2-batch pipelined executor loop (enable_pipelined_scheduler):

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.title: Replace IndexedOrder with ExecutionOrder for MFSDP v2
items.author: shjwudp
items.summary: Replace MFSDP v2's with so repeated calls to one module can have different prefetch successors. For example, in, the two occurrences of lead to and respectively.
items.body:
Replace MFSDP v2's `IndexedOrder` with `ExecutionOrder` so repeated calls to one module can have different prefetch successors. For example, in `A → B → A → C`, the two occurrences of `A` lead to `B` and `C` respectively.

As items are appended, a weak lookup records each unique module's index or marks it as repeated. Unique modules select their position by identity, preserving construction-order behavior for grouped VPP chunk calls. Repeated modules must match the next occurrence at the cursor; a mismatch raises without consuming it. `next_item(offset)` looks ahead without advancing execution

items.title: Fix FP8/FP4 context loss during GDN and KDA recompute
items.author: QiZhangNV
items.summary: When selective recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward.
items.body:
When selective `gdn` recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward. With MXFP8 parameter gathering enabled, this can also cause a missing `main_grad` error.

Use `te_checkpoint` for FP8/FP4 in GDN and KDA to preserve the quantization context, keeping the existing checkpoint path for non-quantized configurations.

Validated with 12 GPU regression cases and a single-node, four-GPU Qwen-style proxy covering MXFP8, NVFP4, and MXFP8 parameter gathering.

items.title: Accumulate the embedding weight gradient into main_grad
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: With gradientaccumulationfusion, VocabParallelEmbedding's backward now adds its weight gradient into maingrad itself, as the linear layers do, and hands autograd a ZeroTensor, so the DDP hook still runs but adds nothing. PyTorch's embedding backward builds a d…
items.body:
With gradient_accumulation_fusion, VocabParallelEmbedding's backward now adds its weight gradient into main_grad itself, as the linear layers do, and hands autograd a ZeroTensor, so the DDP hook still runs but adds nothing. PyTorch's embedding backward builds a dense [vocab, hidden] gradient that the hook then adds whole, about 1 ms per embedding use for a 129280 x 7168 vocabulary on VR200.

For 3073 to 8192 tokens, Triton kernels add only the rows of the tokens that occur, with the arithmetic of PyTorch's sort-based embedding backward followed by main_grad.add_, so main_grad is bit-identical.

items.title: Load the MLA query RoPE dims contiguously in the forward kernel
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Replaces non-contiguous stride-2 RoPE loads with a single contiguous load in the MLA forward kernel, cutting kernel latency from 18.7 μs to 11.3 μs on VR200 for DeepSeek-V3.
items.body:
The in-place query RoPE forward (_mla_rope_fwd_inplace_kernel) read the emb_dim RoPE elements of every head with two stride-2 loads, one for the even and one for the odd elements, and with remove_interleaving it wrote them back with two stride-2 stores. It now loads them with one contiguous load and splits the even and odd elements in registers, and writes the remove_interleaving output with one contiguous store. For DeepSeek-V3's query, [4096, 1, 128, 192] in bf16, the kernel takes 11.3 us instead of 18.7 us on VR200.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When FSDP score centering processes a recorded sampler head, the head-scoring helper and sampled-token CE currently normalize the same vocabulary separately. ### What does this PR do?

此 PR 添加了一个**跨仓库自动文档翻译工作流**（`schedule_doc_translate_ascend.yaml`），它能自动将 `docs/ascend_tutorial/zh/` 下的中文文档翻译为 `docs/ascend_tutorial/en/` 下的英文文档，并按周计划执行。

3. **翻译（Translate）** — 运行 `translate_md.py`，将每个中文文档拆分为块，复用 `.po` 文件中的缓存翻译，仅对更改/未翻译的块调用 OpenAI 兼容的

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ToolAgentLoop._call_tool` runs `create`, `execute` and `release` for every tool call. A `BaseTool` therefore cannot keep state from one turn to the next, although `BaseTool.create` is documented as creating "a tool instance for a trajectory" and `docs/sglang_multiturn/multiturn.rst` points to `BaseTool` for per-trajectory state such as sandbox VMs, scratch directories and DB rows.

This PR creates the instance on the first call to a tool, reuses it for the rest of the trajectory, and releases every instance once when the trajectory ends, including when it raises.

On ARM hosts (e.g. Atlas A2 machines), the vLLM 0.23 scheduler busy-wait with `sched_yield` in `vllm.distributed.utils` degrades badly and causes CPU spin in NPU training jobs. Choose the substitute only when `ABC` actually precedes `nn.Module` in the

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

items.author: yuyz-cyber

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

items.author: Henry-Jessie
items.summary: This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss. Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

items.body:
`abort()` ordered the worker calls as pause → drain → resume, which can hang the rollout under `--partial-rollout` with continuously-submitting (e.g. multi-turn) rollouts.

The call to `/pause?mode=abort` aborts the known requests but leaves the engine in`PAUSED_NEW` status, so a `/generate` POST that races in after the pause ends up in the waiting queue and never returns. One such request blocks the `while state.pendings` drain forever - and `/resume`, the only thing that frees it, sat after the drain.

## Summary

- Fix `TAU_CONFIGS` in the tau-bench example to use `agent_strategy` instead of `agent`.
- Update the README snippet to match.

tau-bench's `RunConfig` defines `agent_strategy`, not `agent`. The previous key was silently ignored by Pydantic, so changing the agent type in `TAU_CONFIGS` had no effect (the default `tool-calling` was always used). `resolve_tau_config()` also accessed `tau_config.agent`, which raises `AttributeError` at rollout time.

Same fix as THUDM/slime#2101.

## Test plan

- [x] `RunConfig(**TAU_CONFIGS)` accepts the config without extra/ignored fields
- [x] Setti

## Summary

Port delta weight sync from slime #1806 (core) and #1991 (CI test + zero-delta version bump).

Bandwidth-optimized weight sync for non-colocate: trainer bytewise-diffs weights against a pinned-CPU snapshot, ships only changed positions+values via nccl broadcast or shared-FS safetensors. Three position encodings (indices/deltas/deltas_zstd). Receiver overwrites changed bytes losslessly.
